---
title: "Train a network"
description: "Prepare a simulated corpus and train one amortized PyMC MFM network."
---

## Corpus contract

Training consumes one or more simulated corpora. A corpus is a dictionary of NumPy arrays for `N` simulated worlds. Every world shares `T`; `K`, `M`, and `J` are padded channel, control, and latent widths. Masks mark represented slots, and padded slots are zero in every array.

| Key | Shape | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `treatment_raw` | `[N, T, K]` | Media spend, `>= 0` |
| `covariates` | `[N, T, M]` | Controls |
| `outcome_raw` | `[N, T]` | Outcome; positive in context |
| `support_mask` | `[N, T]` | `1` for context then `0` for query; both parts are nonempty |
| `treatment_active_mask` | `[N, K]` | Real channels; at least one per world |
| `covariate_active_mask` | `[N, M]` | Real controls; at least one per world |
| `latent_active_mask` | `[N, J]` | Real latent factors |
| `baseline_intrinsic` | `[N, T]` | True baseline |
| `treatment_contribution_raw` | `[N, T, K]` | True channel contributions, `>= 0` |
| `covariate_contribution` | `[N, T, M]` | True control contributions |
| `latent_unobserved_contribution` | `[N, T, J]` | True latent contributions |
| `indirect_effects_by_source` | `[N, T, 3]` | True indirect effects, ordered `cc`, `zc`, `dc` |
| `outcome_noise` | `[N, T]` | Observation noise |
| `g` | `[N, L]` | Binary true causal graph |
| `is_val` | `[N]` | `1` for held-out evaluation worlds; at least one is required |
| `cell_id` | `[N]` | Integer group of related worlds; keep a group in one split |
| `diagnostics` | `dict` | `{"schema_version": 4, "edge_types": ["cy", "dc", "dz", "dy", "zy", "zc", "cc", "zz"]}` |

The listed components plus `outcome_noise` add to `outcome_raw`. Worlds with `is_val == 0` train the network; worlds with `is_val == 1` evaluate it.

## Graph edge blocks

`g` concatenates source-major edge blocks. Its total length is `L`; `EdgeSlotLayout(K, M, J).n_slots` returns that value.

| Block | Edges | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cy` | channel → outcome | `K` |
| `dc` | latent → channel | `J·K` |
| `dz` | latent → control | `J·M` |
| `dy` | latent → outcome | `J` |
| `zy` | control → outcome | `M` |
| `zc` | control → channel | `M·K` |
| `cc` | channel → channel, no self-loops | `K·(K-1)` |
| `zz` | control → control, no self-loops | `M·(M-1)` |

## Run training

Install the training extra, then call [train](../reference/training.train.qmd) with a new output directory. Pass a [ModelConfig](../reference/model.ModelConfig.qmd) for architecture and corpus geometry plus a [TrainingConfig](../reference/training.TrainingConfig.qmd) for the run budget.

```bash
pip install "pymc-mfm[training] @ git+https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-mfm.git"
```

```python
from pymc_mfm import ModelConfig
from pymc_mfm.training import TrainingConfig, train

result = train(
    [corpus],
    out_dir="runs/my-model",
    model_config=ModelConfig(
        n_controls=corpus["covariates"].shape[2],
        n_demand=corpus["latent_active_mask"].shape[1],
    ),
    training=TrainingConfig(
        steps=5_000,
        batch_size=64,
        warmup_steps=250,
        eval_every=1_000,
        milestone_steps=(),
    ),
    device="auto",
)
model = result.model
```

`device="auto"` prefers CUDA, then MPS, then CPU. All supplied corpora must share the same padded `K`, `M`, `J`, and `T` geometry.

## Defaults

[ModelConfig](../reference/model.ModelConfig.qmd) holds architecture size and corpus geometry. It does not fix the channel count.

| `ModelConfig` field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `d_model`, `n_layers`, `n_heads`, `d_ff`, `flow_hidden` | `128`, `4`, `8`, `512`, `256` |
| `n_controls` | `6` |
| `n_demand` | `1` |

[TrainingConfig](../reference/training.TrainingConfig.qmd) defines the canonical full run.

| `TrainingConfig` setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Updates and batch size | `62,500` AdamW updates of `64` worlds |
| Learning rate and schedule | peak `2.8e-3`, `3,125` warmup updates, cosine decay to zero |
| Regularization | weight decay `0.01`; global gradient clipping `1.0` |
| Evaluation | every `6,250` updates on `16` held-out worlds with `128` draws |
| Milestones and seed | updates `25,000` and `50,000`; seed `31` |
| Checkpoint selection | held-out conditional query energy score, with context and structure gates |

For shorter runs, reduce `warmup_steps`, `eval_every`, and `milestone_steps` together with `steps`.

## Tracking, CLI, and outputs

MLflow tracking is enabled by default. Local JSON evidence remains authoritative; MLflow receives a projection of it. By default its SQLite store is in `out_dir`; set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` or [TrackingConfig](../reference/training.TrackingConfig.qmd) `tracking_uri` to choose another backend. Disable tracking with `tracking=TrackingConfig(enabled=False)`.

```bash
python -m pymc_mfm.training --help
```

The CLI exposes the same training options. It reads `.npz` corpora and requires the `generation` extra.

| Path in `out_dir` | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `model/` | Final model folder |
| `checkpoint_best.pt` | Best qualifying held-out checkpoint, written after a promotion |
| `checkpoint_last.pt` | Latest checkpoint |
| `run.json` | Configuration, corpus summary, and run status |
| `metrics.jsonl`, `evaluations.jsonl` | Training losses and held-out evaluations |

Checkpoints do not hold optimizer state and cannot resume a training run. For bitwise-repeatable CPU runs, set `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` before starting the process.
